title: Cocaine toxicity
definition: Sympathomimetic + local anesthetic effects; blocks NE/DA reuptake.
keyPoints: Toxicity: agitation, hyperthermia, HTN, tachycardia, MI, stroke, arrhythmia, seizure
Avoid beta-blockers alone (unopposed alpha worsens HTN)
Treatment: benzodiazepines first-line, phentolamine for HTN, cooling, IV fluids
clinicalContext: Young cocaine user with chest pain, BP 200/120, HR 140, agitation.
nursingPriority: IV lorazepam 2 mg for agitation + BP, avoid pure beta-blocker, consider phentolamine or nitroglycerin, cooling, ECG serial, troponin.

title: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) toxicity
keyPoints: Toxic dose: >150 mg/kg adult, >200 mg/kg child; chronic 4 g/d max
Stages: 1 asymptomatic, 2 RUQ pain 24-72 h, 3 fulminant hepatic failure 72-96 h, 4 recovery or death
Rumack-Matthew nomogram for level at 4 h
Antidote: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) IV 150 mg/kg loading, most effective <8 h
pearls: Don't wait for level if clear toxic ingestion >8 h.
clinicalContext: Intentional overdose of 30 x 500 mg paracetamol tablets 2 h ago.
nursingPriority: Activated charcoal if <1-2 h, 4-h acetaminophen level, start IV NAC 150 mg/kg in 200 mL D5W over 60 min, then 50 mg/kg over 4 h, then 100 mg/kg over 16 h, admit.

title: Carbon monoxide poisoning
definition: Binds Hb with 240x affinity; cherry-red lips.
keyPoints: Source: fire, faulty heaters, auto exhaust
Treatment: 100% O2 reduces t1/2 from 4-5 h to 1 h; hyperbaric O2 for severe/pregnant
pearls: SpO2 cannot distinguish oxyhemoglobin from COHb.
clinicalContext: Family rescued from house fire, confused, cherry-red skin, SpO2 98% on RA.
nursingPriority: Apply 100% non-rebreather mask regardless of SpO2, send COHb level, consider HBOT if severe/pregnant/LOC.

title: Digoxin toxicity
keyPoints: Precipitants: renal failure, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hypercalcemia, amiodarone, verapamil
Symptoms: nausea, yellow-green vision, bradycardia, arrhythmia (AV block, VT)
clinicalContext: Elderly on digoxin + furosemide with nausea, yellow vision, HR 40, level 4.
nursingPriority: Hold digoxin, correct K+/Mg+, atropine for bradycardia, digoxin-specific Fab for severe arrhythmia or K+ >5.5, avoid cardioversion unless essential.

title: Magnesium toxicity in eclampsia
keyPoints: Loading: 4 g IV + 10 g IM (Pritchard) or 4-6 g IV + 1-2 g/h infusion (Zuspan)
Toxicity: 1st loss of DTR (>7), respiratory depression (>10), cardiac arrest (>13)
Antidote: calcium gluconate 1 g IV over 10 min
clinicalContext: Eclamptic on MgSO4 with RR 10, absent DTR.
nursingPriority: Stop MgSO4, give calcium gluconate 1 g IV over 5-10 min, support ventilation, reassess Mg level.

title: Organophosphorus poisoning
keyPoints: SLUDGE: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI upset, Emesis
DUMBELS: Defecation, Urination, Miosis, Bradycardia/bronchorrhea, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation/sweating
Treatment: decontaminate, atropine (dry secretions goal), pralidoxime (oxime)
clinicalContext: Farmer with miosis, drooling, fasciculations, bradycardia, pesticide smell.
nursingPriority: Remove clothing, wash skin + decontaminate staff PPE, atropine 2-4 mg IV repeat doubling q5 min until secretions dry, pralidoxime 30 mg/kg IV, ICU.

title: Antidotes — table
nursingPriority: Naloxone 0.4 mg IV (titrate), support ventilation, continuous monitoring — antidote half-life shorter than opioids may require redosing.

title: Antiplatelet drugs
keyPoints: GP IIb/IIIa: abciximab, eptifibatide — IV, ACS/PCI
DAPT for 12 mo after ACS/DES typically
nursingPriority: DAPT — aspirin 75 mg + ticagrelor 90 mg BD x12 mo minimum, then aspirin alone long-term, PPI if GI risk.

title: Thrombolytic therapy — side effects
keyPoints: Contraindications: prior ICH, stroke <3 mo, head trauma <3 mo, aortic dissection, recent major surgery
Stroke: alteplase 0.9 mg/kg <4.5 h; STEMI: within 30 min of presentation if PCI unavailable
clinicalContext: STEMI within 2 h, no cath lab, no contraindications.
nursingPriority: IV tenecteplase weight-based bolus over 5 s, then aspirin + clopidogrel + enoxaparin, monitor for bleeding, transfer for rescue PCI if failed.

title: Emergency treatment of hypotension
keyPoints: Assess cause: hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive, obstructive
If not responsive: vasopressor — NE first-line for septic/distributive; dopamine if bradycardic; epi for anaphylaxis
clinicalContext: Septic patient BP 75/40 after 30 mL/kg crystalloid.
nursingPriority: Start norepinephrine 0.05-0.1 mcg/kg/min via central line, titrate to MAP >=65, add vasopressin if needed; look for source control.

title: Vasoconstrictor vs vasodilator
keyPoints: Vasoconstrictors: NE, epinephrine, phenylephrine, vasopressin, ergotamine
Vasodilators: nitroglycerin, nitroprusside, hydralazine, nitrates, CCB (amlodipine), nesiritide
clinicalContext: Flash pulmonary edema needing afterload reduction.
nursingPriority: IV nitroglycerin (venous + arterial), titrate, monitor BP.

title: Digoxin
definition: Na-K ATPase inhibitor → increased intracellular Ca → positive inotropy; also vagal → negative chronotropy.
keyPoints: Indications: HF with reduced EF, rate control in AF
Dose: load 0.5 mg IV then 0.25 mg q6 h x2 (total 1-1.5 mg), maintain 0.125-0.25 mg/d
nursingPriority: Add digoxin loading dose IV, monitor ECG continuously, check baseline K+/Mg+/creatinine.

title: Routes of drug administration
keyPoints: Parenteral: SC, IM, IV, ID, intrathecal, epidural
Topical, transdermal, inhaled, intra-articular, ophthalmic, otic
nursingPriority: IV heparin gives immediate effect; LMWH SC slower onset; PO anticoagulants slower still.

title: Adrenaline dose ratios
keyPoints: 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL): IV, cardiac arrest 1 mg q3-5 min
nursingPriority: 1:1000 epinephrine 0.5 mg IM lateral thigh (adult), repeat q5-15 min, call rapid response, IV crystalloid, O2, antihistamine + steroid adjunct.

title: Mydriasis and miotics
nursingPriority: Pilocarpine 2% drops, timolol, IV acetazolamide, analgesia; urgent ophthalmology.

title: Anticholinergic drugs
keyPoints: Examples: atropine, scopolamine, tropicamide, glycopyrrolate, ipratropium, tiotropium, benztropine, oxybutynin
Effects: dry mouth, blurry vision, tachycardia, urinary retention, constipation, mydriasis, hyperthermia
Toxicity: hot as hare, red as beet, blind as bat, dry as bone, mad as hatter
nursingPriority: Atropine IV 2-4 mg, repeat doubling until secretions dry; pralidoxime.

title: Atropine
keyPoints: Bradyarrhythmia: 0.5 mg IV q3-5 min (max 3 mg adult)
OP poisoning: 2-4 mg IV repeat doubling
Side effects: tachycardia, dry mouth, urinary retention, heat intolerance
nursingPriority: Atropine 0.5 mg IV push, repeat q3-5 min up to 3 mg, monitor rhythm, consider transcutaneous pacing if no response.

title: Anaphylaxis — treatment
keyPoints: Criteria: airway/breathing + circulation + skin/mucosa, 2-organ within minutes-hours of exposure
First-line: IM epinephrine 0.5 mg (adult) lateral thigh q5-15 min
Adjunct: O2, crystalloid bolus, antihistamine (H1 + H2), steroid, bronchodilator
clinicalContext: Wasp sting with urticaria, wheeze, BP 80/50.
nursingPriority: IM epinephrine 0.5 mg lateral mid-thigh immediately, call rapid response, high-flow O2, IV crystalloid 1 L bolus, supine with legs up, repeat epi q5-15 min PRN.

title: Antidiarrheal agents
keyPoints: Loperamide: μ-opioid, slow motility; avoid in invasive diarrhea/IBD with toxic mega
nursingPriority: Oral rehydration first, loperamide 4 mg then 2 mg per loose stool (max 16 mg/d), avoid if fever/bloody stool.

title: Proton pump inhibitors (PPI)
keyPoints: Examples: omeprazole, pantoprazole, esomeprazole, rabeprazole, lansoprazole
Long-term: B12/Ca deficiency, C diff, fractures, AKI
PO 20-40 mg OD standard; IV 80 mg bolus + 8 mg/h for bleeding
nursingPriority: PPI 30-60 min before breakfast, re-evaluate in 4-8 wk, step-down once controlled.

title: Carminatives
keyPoints: Not effective in serious underlying pathology
nursingPriority: Simethicone 20-40 mg up to QID, parent reassurance, feeding review; rule out organic pathology.

title: Antiemetics — MOA and use
keyPoints: 5-HT3 antagonists: ondansetron — CINV, PONV; QT prolongation
D2 antagonists: metoclopramide, prochlorperazine — EPS risk
H1 antihistamines: promethazine, meclizine, cyclizine — motion sickness
nursingPriority: Ondansetron 4 mg IV, hydration, consider dexamethasone IV in non-diabetic; monitor for QT.

title: First-line treatment for pulmonary TB
keyPoints: New case regimen: 2HRZE + 4HRE (daily FDC); India shifted to daily from 2017
nursingPriority: Start 4-FDC (HRZE) as per 56-70 kg band daily x2 mo intensive, then 2 drug continuation 4 mo, Nikshay, follow-up sputum at 2 and 6 mo.

title: Side effects of anti-TB drugs
keyPoints: Isoniazid: hepatitis, peripheral neuropathy (give pyridoxine 10 mg)
Rifampicin: orange-red body fluids, hepatitis, enzyme inducer
clinicalContext: Patient on ATT 3 mo with decreased vision.
nursingPriority: Suspect ethambutol optic neuritis — stop EMB, ophthalmology, Snellen + color vision, usually reversible.

title: Tetracycline
keyPoints: Uses: acne, Chlamydia, Rickettsia, Lyme, Brucella, H pylori
Adverse: tooth staining/enamel hypoplasia (avoid <8 y), photosensitivity, esophagitis (take standing with water)
clinicalContext: Pregnant woman with mild acne wants antibiotic.
nursingPriority: Avoid tetracycline — teratogenic to teeth and bones; alternatives erythromycin topical.

title: Antimalarials
keyPoints: Chloroquine: Pv/Po (where CQ-sensitive), hemolysis in G6PD
Primaquine: radical cure Pv/Po, hemolysis in G6PD
nursingPriority: IV artesunate 2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12, 24 h then daily; ICU support; avoid artesunate monotherapy oral.

title: Cephalosporins — generations
nursingPriority: Ampicillin + cefotaxime IV as empirical cover, blood cultures before, monitor renal function.

title: Fentanyl
definition: Synthetic opioid, 100x more potent than morphine.
keyPoints: Respiratory depression, chest wall rigidity (rapid IV)
Uses: anesthesia, severe pain, PCA, transdermal patch for chronic pain
clinicalContext: Chronic pain patient on fentanyl patch develops RR 6.
nursingPriority: Remove patch, naloxone 0.04-0.4 mg IV titrated, support ventilation, continuous monitoring (opioid t1/2 longer than naloxone).

title: Thiopental sodium (Pentothal)
nursingPriority: Avoid thiopental (histamine release); choose ketamine instead.

title: Gaseous anesthetics
nursingPriority: Sevoflurane inhalational induction (non-pungent) with N2O, then IV access.

title: General anesthesia — stages
keyPoints: Modern IV induction bypasses stages rapidly
nursingPriority: Identify stage III as target for surgery.

title: Spinal anesthesia position and complications
keyPoints: Complications: hypotension (sympathetic block), headache (PDPH), urinary retention, total spinal
Nurse: pre-load fluids, monitor BP q2-5 min initially, keep supine for cord block level, foley
clinicalContext: CS patient under spinal with BP drop 80/40.
nursingPriority: Left lateral tilt (avoid aortocaval compression), IV fluid bolus, phenylephrine or ephedrine, O2, call anesthetist.

title: Regional anesthesia
definition: Nerve blocks (peripheral, plexus) and neuraxial (spinal, epidural).
keyPoints: Brachial plexus blocks: interscalene (shoulder), supraclavicular, axillary
nursingPriority: Monitor BP q15 min, assess sensory level, check for urinary retention, left lateral tilt, maternal positioning.

title: Diuretics — classes
keyPoints: Loop (furosemide, torsemide, bumetanide): inhibit NKCC2 in thick ascending limb — most potent
K-sparing (spironolactone, eplerenone, amiloride): collecting duct; gynecomastia spironolactone
nursingPriority: Furosemide 40 mg IV, nitroglycerin drip, upright position, O2, BiPAP if respiratory fatigue.

title: Furosemide (Lasix)
clinicalContext: IV furosemide 80 mg bolus for pulmonary edema.
nursingPriority: Administer over 1-2 min (ototoxicity risk with rapid push), monitor K+, check weight/UO, correct K+ with IV KCl if <3.5.

title: Insulin — types, onset, peak, duration
keyPoints: Rapid (lispro, aspart, glulisine): 10-15 min / 1-2 h / 3-5 h
nursingPriority: Basal glargine OD bedtime + rapid (aspart) before meals, carb counting, monitor BG 4x/d, rotate sites.

title: Anticancer drugs — classes
keyPoints: Alkylating: cyclophosphamide (hemorrhagic cystitis, use mesna), cisplatin (nephrotoxic, ototoxic)
nursingPriority: Ensure adequate hydration + mesna to prevent hemorrhagic cystitis, antiemetic, monitor CBC.

title: Dose calculation — adult and pediatric
keyPoints: Pediatric: mg/kg or mg/m2 (BSA more accurate for chemo)
BSA Mosteller: √((ht cm x wt kg)/3600)
Young rule: age/(age+12) x adult dose
nursingPriority: Dose = 200 mg; draw up from suspension concentration and double-check.

title: Flow rate and drops/min calculations
keyPoints: Drops/min = (volume mL x drop factor) / time (min)
clinicalContext: 500 mL NS over 4 h with 15 gtt/mL set.
nursingPriority: Drops/min = (500 x 15) / 240 = 31 gtt/min.

title: Drug of choice table
nursingPriority: Recall as per indication table.

title: Alcohol withdrawal symptoms — CIWA-Ar
keyPoints: Timeline: tremor 6-12 h, seizure 12-48 h, hallucinations 12-48 h, DTs 48-96 h
DT: autonomic hyperactivity, confusion, visual hallucinations
Treatment: benzodiazepine symptom-triggered (CIWA >=10), thiamine IM/IV before dextrose (prevent Wernicke), fluids
clinicalContext: Alcoholic 36 h after last drink, tremor, tachycardia, diaphoresis.
nursingPriority: CIWA-Ar score, thiamine 100 mg IV before glucose, benzodiazepine (lorazepam) per CIWA, IV fluid, monitor vitals.

title: Malignant hypertension — pharmacologic management
keyPoints: Target organ damage: AKI, encephalopathy, heart failure
Reduce MAP 10-25% first hour, then to 160/100 over 2-6 h
nursingPriority: ICU admit, IV labetalol bolus + infusion, reduce MAP 10-25% in 1 h, monitor hourly, workup secondary causes.

title: Beta-blockers — cautions
keyPoints: Bradycardia, AV block, hypotension, bronchospasm, fatigue, depression, sexual dysfunction, masked hypoglycemia
Avoid: asthma (non-selective), severe peripheral disease, heart block > 1st degree, decompensated HF (use cautiously when stable)
nursingPriority: Avoid non-selective beta-blocker; choose ACE-i/ARB or CCB instead.

title: ACE inhibitors — side effects
keyPoints: Side effects: dry cough (bradykinin), hyperkalemia, AKI in RAS, angioedema (life-threatening), teratogenic
Hold if K+ >5.5 or creatinine rises >30%
clinicalContext: HTN patient develops dry cough on enalapril.
nursingPriority: Switch to ARB (losartan) which avoids bradykinin-mediated cough.

title: Warfarin — INR targets
definition: Vit K antagonist; inhibits factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C, S.
keyPoints: Bleeding reversal: vit K + PCC + FFP
Initial paradoxical hypercoagulability — overlap with heparin 5 d and INR >=2
clinicalContext: Patient on warfarin with INR 8, no bleeding.
nursingPriority: Hold warfarin, low-dose oral vit K 1-2 mg, recheck INR in 24 h, investigate cause (diet, drug).

title: Heparin — monitoring
keyPoints: UFH: IV infusion, monitor aPTT (1.5-2x normal)
LMWH (enoxaparin): SC, no routine monitoring, anti-Xa in special populations
Antidote: protamine sulfate (1 mg/100 U UFH; partial for LMWH)
HIT: stop heparin, switch to non-heparin anticoag
clinicalContext: PE on UFH with platelets drop 50% at day 5.
nursingPriority: Suspect HIT — stop all heparin, send HIT antibody + SRA, start non-heparin anticoagulant (argatroban or fondaparinux), avoid transfusion.

title: Lithium — therapeutic range
keyPoints: Toxicity: >1.5 tremor, nausea, ataxia; >2.5 seizure, coma
Renal elimination — NSAIDs, thiazides, ACE-i increase levels; sodium depletion worsens
Side effects: polyuria, hypothyroidism, weight gain, nephrotoxicity
clinicalContext: Bipolar patient on lithium + NSAID with tremor, confusion, level 3.2.
nursingPriority: Stop lithium, hydrate with IV NS, stop offending drugs, consider hemodialysis if severe, monitor Na+/K+/cr.

title: Phenytoin — side effects
keyPoints: Side effects: gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism, coarsening of features, megaloblastic anemia (folate), osteomalacia, teratogenic (fetal hydantoin)
clinicalContext: Epileptic on phenytoin develops gum overgrowth.
nursingPriority: Excellent dental hygiene, dental review, consider alternative agent, check drug level.

title: Morphine — respiratory depression
keyPoints: Side effects: respiratory depression, hypotension, miosis, constipation, pruritus, urinary retention, biliary spasm
Avoid in severe renal failure (metabolite accumulation)
clinicalContext: Cancer pain patient on morphine with RR 8.
nursingPriority: Titrated naloxone 0.04 mg IV, support ventilation, reassess, reconsider pain regimen.

title: Naloxone
keyPoints: Dose: 0.04-0.4 mg IV titrated; IM if no IV
Half-life shorter than most opioids — may need repeat or infusion
Precipitates acute withdrawal in chronic users
clinicalContext: Opioid overdose with RR 6, pinpoint pupils.
nursingPriority: 0.04-0.4 mg IV naloxone titrated to respiration (not full wakefulness) to avoid severe withdrawal, support ventilation, continuous monitoring.

title: Nitroglycerin
keyPoints: Sublingual 0.3-0.6 mg x3 q5 min for angina
IV for acute pulmonary edema, HTN emergency
Side effects: headache, hypotension, reflex tachycardia, tolerance (need nitrate-free interval)
Contraindications: hypotension, inferior MI with RV infarction, recent sildenafil
clinicalContext: Angina patient takes sildenafil yesterday, now chest pain.
nursingPriority: Avoid nitroglycerin (severe hypotension with PDE-5 inhibitors); use alternative (morphine, O2, assessment).

title: Drug allergy — first sign
clinicalContext: Patient develops hives 10 min after IV antibiotic.
nursingPriority: Stop antibiotic, antihistamine, observe for anaphylaxis progression, document allergy, report ADR.

title: Look-alike sound-alike (LASA) drugs
definition: LASA pairs to prevent medication errors.
nursingPriority: Verbal readback, TALL-MAN letters, double-check on MAR, avoid confusing HYDROXYZINE.

title: High alert medications
definition: Meds with high risk of patient harm if error.
keyPoints: Insulin, heparin, opioids, chemo, concentrated electrolytes (KCl), neuromuscular blockers, anticoagulants
Independent double-check, standardized concentrations, limit stock, bar-coding
nursingPriority: Independent double-check: right patient, drug, dose, route, rate, never IV push concentrated KCl, use central line for high concentrations.

title: Safe syringe disposal
keyPoints: Puncture-resistant white translucent container per BMW Rules 2016
Do NOT recap (or use one-hand scoop)
nursingPriority: Do not recap, drop directly into white translucent sharps bin, never fill >3/4.

title: Insulin sliding scale
keyPoints: Modern guidelines discourage sliding scale alone — use basal-bolus for inpatients
Check BG q4-6 h or before meals
nursingPriority: Give correction per institutional basal-bolus protocol, reassess in 2-4 h, adjust basal if persistent hyperglycemia.

title: Vaccine diluent and storage
keyPoints: BCG: NS provided with vial; discard after 4 h
clinicalContext: BCG reconstituted 2 h ago; session continues.
nursingPriority: Use within 4 h of reconstitution; discard if beyond; store in cold box at 2-8°C during session.

title: Reconstitution of drugs
nursingPriority: Use sterile water 10 mL for IV, label with date/time/initials, use within hours per insert, verify compatibility with IV solution.

title: Drug-drug interaction basics
keyPoints: Pharmacokinetic: absorption (antacids), distribution (protein binding), metabolism (CYP induction/inhibition), excretion
clinicalContext: Patient on warfarin started on clarithromycin.
nursingPriority: Clarithromycin CYP3A4 inhibitor — raises warfarin level; monitor INR closely, consider alternative macrolide (azithromycin) if possible.

title: Medication error reporting
keyPoints: ADR reporting to PvPI via ADR form
Anonymized data to ISMP, national PSC
nursingPriority: Disclose to patient, monitor BG frequently, document, file incident report, RCA to identify systemic improvement; non-punitive culture.
